pages.class_justification: No construction is involved: one fixed reduction runs any LWE distinguisher as an oracle on the succinct-LWE challenge, forwarding $(\mathbf{B}, \mathbf{u}_b)$ and discarding $(\mathbf{W}, T)$. This is the RTV04 fully-black-box shape, and matches how the wiki records other assumption-strengthening edges (e.g. strong RSA implies RSA).
pages.statement: Hardness of $\ell$-[[learning-with-errors#succinct-lwe|succinct LWE]] implies hardness of [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] for the same $(n, q, \chi, m)$: the succinct-LWE adversary is handed the LWE challenge $(\mathbf{B}, \mathbf{u}_b)$ together with $(\mathbf{W}, T)$, which it may discard, and the $\mathbf{B}$ produced by $\mathrm{TrapGen}$ is statistically close to uniform. The converse is known only at $\ell = 1$; for $\ell > 1$ succinct LWE is not known to follow from LWE, and the assumption strengthens as $\ell$ grows — folklore.
pages.sketch: Any LWE distinguisher $\calA$ becomes a succinct-LWE distinguisher that runs $\calA$ on $(\mathbf{B}, \mathbf{u}_b)$ and ignores the trapdoor terms $(\mathbf{W}, T)$; the only loss is the statistical distance between $\mathrm{TrapGen}$'s output and uniform.
pages.security_loss: advantage-preserving up to the statistical distance between $\mathrm{TrapGen}(1^n,1^m,q)$'s $\mathbf{B}$ and uniform
flags: HIGH PRIORITY: the frontmatter `kind: equivalence`, the `title` and the H1 all assert an unqualified 'Succinct LWE ⇔ LWE'. That is false: the migrated paragraph itself says the assumption strengthens as $\ell$ grows, and $\ell$-succinct LWE for $\ell > 1$ is not known to follow from LWE (Wee obtains it from public-coin evasive LWE). Set kind: implication and retitle to 'Succinct LWE ⇒ LWE'; the slug succinct-lwe-to-lwe still fits, so no URL change is needed.

The migrated justification is wrong in detail and belongs to the skeptical-checker lane: content/Assumptions/learning-with-errors.md § Succinct LWE says that at $\ell = 1$ 'there is no $\mathbf{W}$ block and $T$ reduces to $T_\mathbf{B}$ itself'. At $\ell = 1$ the block $\mathbf{W} \in \ZZ_q^{n \times m}$ is still present ($[\mathbf{B} \mid \mathbf{W}] T = \mathbf{G}$ with $T \in \ZZ^{2m \times m}$), and handing the adversary a gadget trapdoor $T_\mathbf{B}$ for $\mathbf{B}$ would make the game trivially losable ($\mathbf{u} T_\mathbf{B} = \mathbf{s}\mathbf{G} + \mathbf{e}T_\mathbf{B}$ recovers $\mathbf{s}$), not equivalent to LWE. The $\ell = 1$ equivalence instead follows because $(\mathbf{B}, \mathbf{W}, T)$ can be sampled from a uniform (externally supplied) $\mathbf{B}$ by generating $\mathbf{W}$ with its own trapdoor and using it to sample $T$.

The $\ell = 1$ converse is left uncited in the statement: eprint.iacr.org, link.springer.com and arxiv.org are blocked by this environment's egress proxy, so Wee25/Wee24 could not be opened to confirm the claim. If a human can check Wee25, the sentence should end with the Wee25 citation instead of relying on '— folklore'.
Batch red-31 (succinct-lwe-to-evasive-lwe) independently flagged this page for exactly this over-claim; the two dispositions agree.

pages.wrong_reason: The edge is not well posed over the wiki's own definitions, and the migrated sentence does not state it. SXDH is an assumption about Type-3 (asymmetric) pairings — DDH is hard in both $\GG_1$ and $\GG_2$ — whereas content/Assumptions/bilinear-map-assumptions.md defines both BDH and BDDH for a symmetric pairing $e : \GG \times \GG \to \GG_T$. In a symmetric pairing DDH in $\GG$ is broken by the pairing itself ($e(g^a, g^b) = e(g, g^{ab})$), so SXDH is false there and the two assumptions are not stated over the same group family; this is exactly the imprecision the page's own migration note records. Separately, the only directional content in the migrated text is 'Stronger than BDDH', which concerns the *decisional* BDH assumption, not the computational BDH that the conclusion node `bdh` denotes, and it carries neither an argument nor a citation. Even restricted to Type-3 groups the claim is formulation-dependent: for a DBDH variant whose instance is $(g_1, g_1^a, g_1^b, g_2^c)$ a DDH distinguisher in $\GG_1$ does follow from a DBDH distinguisher, but for the standard variant that also hands the adversary $g_2^a, g_2^b$ no reduction from SXDH is known, since there is no efficient map $\GG_1 \to \GG_2$. No source was found asserting SXDH ⇒ (D)BDH. Do not record this edge until the wiki states BDH/BDDH over an asymmetric pairing and names the variant.
flags: HIGH PRIORITY: recommend deleting this edge, or re-scoping it once content/Assumptions/bilinear-map-assumptions.md states BDH/BDDH in the Type-3 setting. The page's SUSPECTED IMPRECISION note is correct and should survive whatever is done.

Structural defect on the parent page: SXDH is registered as a `variants:` entry of the bdh node, but SXDH is meaningful only for Type-3 pairings while the page's BDH/BDDH games are written for Type-1. Either split the symmetric and asymmetric assumption families or state each game over $\GG_1, \GG_2$.

sources.ref_file_title: GS08 - Efficient Non-interactive Proof Systems for Bilinear Groups
sources.note: Verified in vendor/cryptobib/crypto.bib as EC:GroSah08 (pages 415-432, doi 10.1007/978-3-540-78967-3_24); eprint version EPRINT:GroSah07, Cryptology ePrint Archive Report 2007/155. Use cryptobib_key: EC:GroSah08. Received the IACR Test-of-Time award in 2023.

pages.class_justification: The hypothesis is a hardness assumption over a concrete bilinear group, not a primitive the construction can call as an oracle, so the RTV04 axis does not apply cleanly; GS08 give an algebraic construction and do not classify the reduction. Left unstated, matching the wiki's other assumption-to-primitive edges.
pages.model_justification: Groth-Sahai proofs live in the common reference string model: the CRS is a commitment key, perfectly binding in one mode and perfectly hiding (with a simulation trapdoor) in the other, and SXDH is what makes the two modes indistinguishable.
pages.statement: [[bilinear-map-assumptions#sxdh-symmetric-external-diffie-hellman|SXDH]] over a Type-3 pairing group yields non-interactive witness-indistinguishable proofs and [[non-interactive-zero-knowledge|NIZK]] proofs, in the common reference string model, for satisfiability of systems of pairing-product, multi-scalar-multiplication and quadratic equations over that group; circuit satisfiability encodes into such a system, so every language in $\classNP$ has a NIZK proof whose size grows linearly in the circuit — [[GS08 - Efficient Non-interactive Proof Systems for Bilinear Groups|GS08]]. SXDH is one of the three instantiations GS08 give, alongside the subgroup decision assumption and DLIN.
pages.sketch: The CRS is a key for a homomorphic commitment to group elements and to exponents. Under SXDH the binding key (extractable, giving soundness) and the hiding key (perfectly hiding, with a simulation trapdoor, giving zero knowledge) are computationally indistinguishable, so a proof — commitments to the witness plus a few group elements that make the equation verify after cancellation — is sound under one key and simulatable under the other.
flags: The sibling edge DLIN ⇒ NIZK, also GS08, has no page (content/Reductions/ has only dlin-to-ippe-ksw08.md). The migration note on this page records the duplicate; creating dlin-to-nizk-gs08 with the same GS08 source would complete the family. Subgroup decision ⇒ NIZK is a third GS08 instantiation.

Verification of the GS08 abstract was indirect: eprint.iacr.org, iacr.org, dblp.org, arxiv.org and link.springer.com are all blocked by this environment's egress proxy. Bibliographic data comes from vendor/cryptobib (EC:GroSah08); the three instantiations (subgroup decision, SXDH, DLIN) and the linear-size circuit-satisfiability proofs were confirmed from secondary sources (COSIC and Mysten Labs expositions, Ghadafi-Smart-Warinschi 'Groth-Sahai Proofs Revisited'), not from the paper itself.
GS08 obtain NIZK rather than only NIWI for the equation classes they identify; a full statement of which equation forms admit zero knowledge is a nuance the one-sentence statement omits deliberately.

sources.ref_file_title: AH91 - Statistical zero-knowledge languages can be recognized in two rounds
sources.venue: Journal of Computer and System Sciences 42(3):327-345, 1991
sources.note: Preliminary version: 'Perfect Zero-Knowledge Languages Can Be Recognized in Two Rounds', FOCS 1987, pp. 439-448, doi 10.1109/SFCS.1987.47 (vendor/cryptobib key FOCS:AieHas87). The journal version is the one usually cited for SZK ⊆ AM and is the one titled 'Statistical'; cryptobib carries only the FOCS entry, so the stub needs inline bibtex or cryptobib_key FOCS:AieHas87 with a note.

sources.ref_file_title: SV03 - A Complete Problem for Statistical Zero Knowledge
sources.note: Preliminary version FOCS 1997; Cryptology ePrint Archive Report 2000/056 (cryptobib key EPRINT:SahVad00). The paper's own summary of consequences names 'simpler proofs of many of the previously known results about statistical zero knowledge, such as the Fortnow and Aiello-Hastad upper bounds on the complexity of SZK'.

pages.class_justification: A containment between complexity classes, proved by an unrestricted argument; the reduction-class axis does not discriminate here. Matches the wiki's convention on bpp-to-coam-gs86 and qszk-to-qip.
pages.statement: $\classSZK \subseteq \classAM$: every promise problem with a [[statistical-zero-knowledge|statistical zero-knowledge]] proof system has a two-message public-coin ([[arthur-merlin|Arthur-Merlin]]) proof — [[AH91 - Statistical zero-knowledge languages can be recognized in two rounds|AH91]]. With the companion containment $\classSZK \subseteq \classcoAM$ this places $\classSZK$ inside $\classAM \cap \classcoAM$, so $\classSZK$ contains no $\classNP$-complete problem unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses.
pages.improvements_text: - The $\classSZK$-completeness of the Statistical Difference problem gives a simpler and unified proof of this bound and of $\classSZK \subseteq \classcoAM$ — [[SV03 - A Complete Problem for Statistical Zero Knowledge|SV03]]
flags: Resolves the explicit 'TODO citation' on content/Complexity/co-arthur-merlin.md § Known relationships and the uncited bullet on content/Complexity/statistical-zero-knowledge.md; both should be updated in the same commit (reference-fixer lane), and both write the containment with Unicode ⊆/∩ outside math mode although \classSZK, \classAM, \classcoAM all exist.

AH91 and For87 prove the containments for honest-verifier SZK. HVSZK = SZK is Goldreich-Sahai-Vadhan (STOC 1998), which the wiki has no reference page for; if the honest-verifier distinction is ever stated on these pages, that citation is needed.

Unrelated but adjacent: content/Complexity/statistical-zero-knowledge.md attributes 'SZK is closed under complement' to GS86 (Goldwasser-Sipser, private vs public coins). That result is Okamoto's, not GS86's. Skeptical-checker lane.

sources.ref_file_title: For87 - The Complexity of Perfect Zero-Knowledge
sources.note: Verified in vendor/cryptobib/crypto.bib as STOC:Fortnow87 ('The Complexity of Perfect Zero-Knowledge (Extended Abstract)', pp. 204-209). Use cryptobib_key: STOC:Fortnow87. Reprinted in Advances in Computing Research 5 (ed. Micali), pp. 327-343, 1989, which is why some papers cite it as [For89].

sources.ref_file_title: SV03 - A Complete Problem for Statistical Zero Knowledge
sources.note: Preliminary version FOCS 1997; ePrint 2000/056 (cryptobib key EPRINT:SahVad00). Same entry as proposed on szk-to-am; create the reference page once.

pages.class_justification: A containment between complexity classes, proved by an unrestricted argument. Matches the wiki's convention on bpp-to-coam-gs86 and qszk-to-qip.
pages.statement: $\classSZK \subseteq \classcoAM$: if a promise problem has a [[statistical-zero-knowledge|statistical zero-knowledge]] proof system then its complement has an Arthur-Merlin proof, so the problem lies in [[co-arthur-merlin|coAM]] — [[For87 - The Complexity of Perfect Zero-Knowledge|For87]]. Consequently no $\classNP$-complete problem has a statistical zero-knowledge proof unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses.
pages.improvements_text: - The $\classSZK$-completeness of the Statistical Difference problem gives a simpler and unified proof of this bound and of $\classSZK \subseteq \classAM$ — [[SV03 - A Complete Problem for Statistical Zero Knowledge|SV03]]
flags: For87's title and its theorem are stated for *perfect* zero knowledge; the literature nevertheless cites Fortnow for $\classSZK \subseteq \classcoAM$ (the argument extends to statistical zero knowledge, and SV03 names 'the Fortnow and Aiello-Hastad upper bounds on the complexity of SZK' as results it reproves). The reference page's H1 must keep the paper's real title.
Resolves the 'TODO citation' on content/Complexity/co-arthur-merlin.md; the same line also needs \classcoAM/\classSZK math mode and a wikilink to content/Complexity/statistical-zero-knowledge.md.
Same honest-verifier caveat as szk-to-am: the containment is proved for HVSZK, and HVSZK = SZK is Goldreich-Sahai-Vadhan (STOC 1998), for which the wiki has no reference page.

pages.class_justification: A containment between complexity classes, immediate from the two definitions; the reduction-class axis does not discriminate here.
pages.statement: $\classSZK \subseteq \classCZK$: statistical indistinguishability of the verifier's view from the simulator's output implies computational indistinguishability, so every [[statistical-zero-knowledge|statistical]] zero-knowledge proof system is a [[computational-zero-knowledge|computational]] one with the same protocol and the same simulator — folklore.
flags: The bullet this was migrated from, on content/Complexity/computational-zero-knowledge.md § Known relationships, reads only 'Contains [[statistical-zero-knowledge|SZK]]' with its subject elided and no folklore marker; per the citation policy it should end with '— folklore'. Editor lane.

pages.class_justification: A containment between complexity classes, immediate from the definitions; the reduction-class axis does not discriminate here. Same shape as qszk-to-qip.
pages.statement: $\classSZK \subseteq \classIP$: a statistical zero-knowledge proof system is an [[interactive-proof-systems|interactive proof]] carrying an additional simulation requirement, so dropping that requirement leaves every problem in [[statistical-zero-knowledge|SZK]] inside $\classIP$ — folklore.
flags: The source text never states the relation — it is implicit in 'in such an interactive proof' in the SZK page's intro. The edge is real and definitional; keeping it is right, but content/Complexity/statistical-zero-knowledge.md should state it explicitly in § Known relationships rather than leaving it to be inferred.
$\classIP = \classPSPACE$ on content/Complexity/interactive-proof-systems.md still carries a 'TODO citation' (Shamir 1992 / LFKN 1992). Not this edge, but adjacent.

sources.ref_file_title: Wat02 - Limits on the Power of Quantum Statistical Zero-Knowledge
sources.note: Verified in vendor/cryptobib/crypto.bib as FOCS:Watrous02 (pp. 459-470). NB cryptobib's title field has a typo ('imits on the Power...'); the reference page must use the correct title. Preprint arXiv:quant-ph/0202111, 'Quantum statistical zero-knowledge'. This paper defines honest-verifier QSZK, proves the trace-distance problem complete for it, that it is closed under complement and contained in PSPACE, and establishes the connections to classical SZK.

Verified in vendor/cryptobib/crypto.bib as STOC:Watrous06 (pp. 296-305). Journal version SIAM J. Comput. 39(1):25-58, 2009; the key Wat09 is NOT usable here because content/References/Wat09 - Dual System Encryption... is Waters 2009. Introduces the quantum rewinding lemma and proves that honest-verifier and general-verifier QSZK coincide.

pages.class_justification: A containment between complexity classes; the reduction-class axis does not discriminate here. Matches qszk-to-qip.
pages.model_justification: The conclusion class is defined over quantum verifiers, quantum messages and quantum simulators, so the containment is stated in the quantum model even though the hypothesis class is classical.
pages.statement: $\classSZK \subseteq \classQSZK$: a classical statistical zero-knowledge proof system is a quantum one in which every message and every simulator output is classical, so [[statistical-zero-knowledge|SZK]] is contained in the honest-verifier class Watrous defines — [[Wat02 - Limits on the Power of Quantum Statistical Zero-Knowledge|Wat02]]. The containment extends to [[quantum-statistical-zero-knowledge|QSZK]] against arbitrary quantum verifiers because honest-verifier and general-verifier quantum statistical zero knowledge coincide, proved via the quantum rewinding lemma — [[Wat06 - Zero-knowledge against quantum attacks|Wat06]].
pages.improvements_text: - Removes the honest-verifier restriction: quantum rewinding gives $\mathbf{QSZK}_{\mathrm{HV}} = \classQSZK$, so the classical containment holds against arbitrary quantum verifiers — [[Wat06 - Zero-knowledge against quantum attacks|Wat06]]
flags: Wat02 could not be opened (cs.uwaterloo.ca, arxiv.org, eprint.iacr.org and link.springer.com are blocked by this environment's egress proxy). Its bibliographic data is verified against vendor/cryptobib and its stated results against two independent secondary summaries; the containment itself is immediate from Watrous's definition. If a human finds that Wat02 does not state SZK ⊆ QSZK_HV explicitly, Wat06 alone carries the citation and Wat02 should be demoted to the definitional reference for QSZK.

The page's migration note about quantum rewinding is correct and is now answered: the 'special case of a quantum one' argument is honest and complete only for the honest-verifier class; the general-verifier statement needs Wat06. The one-line justification on content/Complexity/quantum-statistical-zero-knowledge.md § Known relationships should be extended accordingly.

Two further 'TODO citation (Watrous 2002)' markers on content/Complexity/quantum-statistical-zero-knowledge.md (QSD is QSZK-complete; coQSZK = QSZK) are resolved by the same Wat02 reference page — worth fixing in the same commit.

sources.ref_file_title: DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications
sources.authors: Nico Döttling, Sanjam Garg, Yuval Ishai, Giulio Malavolta, Tamer Mour, Rafail Ostrovsky
sources.note: Introduces trapdoor hash functions and the route from them to low-communication PIR: TDH with a one-bit hint gives two-message rate-1 string OT, and thence 'the first constructions of PIR with communication cost poly-logarithmic in the database size based on DDH or QR' (paper abstract, quoted on the wiki's own reference page). This, not AMR25, is the origin of the TDH-to-PIR compiler.

sources.ref_file_title: AMR25 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and PIR from Low-Noise LPN
sources.authors: Damiano Abram, Giulio Malavolta, Lawrence Roy
sources.note: Instantiates the route from a low-noise-LPN trapdoor hash function with compression factor $2^{\Theta(\log^{1-\beta}\secpar)}$, giving PIR with communication $L/2^{\Theta(\log^{1-\beta}L)}$ — the first PIR with non-trivial communication from a code-based assumption. Not the origin of the TDH-to-PIR step.

pages.class_justification: The compiler is generic in the trapdoor hash function, but DGI+19 obtain PIR with polylogarithmic communication only from their DDH- and QR-based instantiations (not from the LWE one), so what the source establishes is not a single construction that turns *any* TDH into non-trivial PIR with a fixed communication bound. Claiming fully-black-box would overstate the source; left unstated, matching the wiki's other DGI+19 edges.
pages.statement: A [[trapdoor-hash-function|trapdoor hash function]] for the index predicates $f_i(x) = x_i$ with a short (one-bit, in the rate-1 case) hint yields two-message rate-1 string [[oblivious-transfer|OT]], and from it [[single-server-private-information-retrieval|single-server PIR]]: from their DDH- and QR-based trapdoor hash functions [[DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications|DGI+19]] obtain PIR with communication $\polylog(n)$ in the database size $n$. The communication achieved is governed by the trapdoor hash function's compression factor: the low-noise-LPN construction of [[AMR25 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and PIR from Low-Noise LPN|AMR25]], with compression $2^{\Theta(\log^{1-\beta}\secpar)}$, gives PIR with communication $L/2^{\Theta(\log^{1-\beta}L)}$ for a database of size $L$.
pages.improvements_text: - The first trapdoor hash function from a code-based assumption, and with it the first single-server PIR with communication asymptotically below $L$ from LPN: quasi-polynomial hardness of low-noise LPN with rate $\varepsilon = O(\log^{1+\beta}(k)/k)$, $\beta > 0$, gives PIR with communication $L/2^{\Theta(\log^{1-\beta}L)}$ — [[AMR25 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and PIR from Low-Noise LPN|AMR25]]
flags: HIGH PRIORITY: the slug carries the suffix `-amr25` but the reduction is DGI+19's; AMR25 only instantiate it. The page's own migration note ('the generic TDH-to-sublinear-PIR compiler is not original to AMR25, so the citation may be misattributed here') is correct. The honest slug is tdh-to-cpir-dgi-19 or an unsuffixed tdh-to-cpir, but renaming changes a live URL — leave the rename to a human and at minimum reorder `source:` so DGI+19 comes first.

The Notes section contains a literal '[object Object]' where the conflicting citations were meant to be listed ('Citations disagree across pages: [object Object]'). Migration bug; should be removed or filled in.

The Notes section is an unmerged concatenation of the notes from all five migrated statements (DDH, QR and LWE branches, plus the sub-bullet), including duplicated lines. It needs rewriting to the one or two caveats that survive, not preserving.

Precision worth keeping in mind if the statement is rewritten: DGI+19 get rate-1 string OT from DDH, QR *or* LWE, but polylogarithmic-communication PIR only from DDH or QR. A blanket 'TDH implies polylog PIR' would be wrong.
'Fully sublinear PIR from any flavour of LPN is open' (nested sub-bullet on content/Assumptions/learning-parity-with-noise.md) is an open problem, not an edge; it should stay on the assumption page.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction that calls $\Gen$ and $\Eval$ as oracles and never inspects their code, and one fixed reduction that runs any inverter for the derived function as an oracle and returns its $x$ component. The RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.statement: A [[trapdoor-permutation|trapdoor permutation]] family $\mathsf{TDP} = (\Gen, \Eval, \Invert)$ yields a one-way function ([[hash-function|OWF]]): define $g(r, x) = (f, \Eval(f, x))$ where $(f, \td) = \Gen(1^\secpar; r)$ and the trapdoor is discarded. Inverting $g$ on $(f, y)$ recovers the unique $x$ with $\Eval(f, x) = y$, contradicting one-wayness of $\mathsf{TDP}$ against an adversary given the index but not $\td$ — folklore.
pages.sketch: The construction just withholds the trapdoor: $\Eval(f, \cdot)$ is a bijection on $\calD$, so any preimage of $(f, y)$ under $g$ contains the unique $\Eval(f, \cdot)$-preimage of $y$, and the reduction outputs it verbatim. The derived $g$ is in fact a one-way permutation on each index.
flags: The conclusion node is `hash-function`, which this wiki uses for OWF, one-way permutation and CRH alike. The sharper true edge is TDP ⇒ OWP, and content/Primitives/one-way-permutation.md exists and is unlinked. Either retarget this edge to one-way-permutation or split an OWF node out of hash-function; until then the conflation is a modelling defect, not a defect of this claim.

Editor-lane defects on the source pages remain: content/Primitives/impagliazzos-five-worlds.md writes '[[trapdoor-permutation|TDFs]] exist → [[hash-function|OWFs]]s exist' (permutation page glossed as trapdoor *functions*, and a stray trailing s), and content/Primitives/trapdoor-permutation.md asserts 'Trapdoor permutations are one-way functions with an additional invertibility structure' with no wikilink to the OWF node.
Imp95 is cited only in the intro of impagliazzos-five-worlds.md, never on the bullet; since this edge is folklore that is acceptable, but the bullet should carry a '— folklore' marker.
